task.description: Validate src/design/iss0612-provisioning-lock-scope-fix.md, a Type E design fixing ISS-0612/GH-556's confirmed root cause: provisionTenantSchema()'s advisory-lock block (provisioning.zig:117-125) closes its own scope before Steps 2-6a (the real work) even begin, so concurrent same-tenant calls race unprotected. The design proposes: (1) restructure so a single lock_conn, acquired once, is reused across Step 2 (idempotency check), Steps 3-4 (bpm_provision_tenant_schema() call), Step 6 (timestamp update), and Step 6a (tenant promotion), with lock release + connection release as one defer pair covering every exit path; (2) Step 5 (runForSchema migrations) deliberately keeps its own separate connection rather than sharing lock_conn, with an explicit deadlock analysis concluding no cross-lock wait-for cycle exists between the tenant-level session lock and MIGRATIONS_LOCK_KEY_SQL's global xact-scoped lock (different connections, disjoint keyspaces); (3) recommends keeping bpm_provision_tenant_schema()'s internal per-schema lock as-is (protects direct SQL callers); (4) recommends adding pg_advisory_unlock_all() to Pool.release() as defense-in-depth. Verify all of this against the actual current source -- do not trust the design doc's or CODE-DESIGNER's own description without checking. This is an architecturally significant change (touches connection/transaction lifecycle in a function multiple other issues (ISS-0131, ISS-0209) already depend on) -- scrutinize the deadlock-freedom claim particularly closely, since a wrong analysis here could trade a hang for a deadlock instead of actually fixing anything.
acceptance_criteria: Design correctly restructures the lock scope to cover Steps 2-6a on a single connection
The deadlock-freedom claim between the tenant session lock and MIGRATIONS_LOCK_KEY_SQL is independently verified against actual source, not just trusted from the design doc
Design addresses the third (per-schema SQL-level) lock layer with a defensible recommendation
Design addresses the Pool.release() defense-in-depth recommendation
